I have farmed these 60 mu for 30 years. I never went to school, but I learned from my father-in-law and from watching the good farmers in our village. I know what works on this land because I have done it with my own hands.

Last year I put one bag of compound fertilizer on every mu of wheat before planting — that is 100 jin per mu. The bag says 18-22-5, which means it has nitrogen, phosphate, and a little potash. Then when the wheat turned green in spring, I spread urea on top, about 50 jin per mu, and I did it again at heading time. That gave me 1000 jin of wheat per mu. This year I will do the same thing. Fertilizer costs more now, but I would rather spend a little too much than risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest means I cannot pay for my grandson's school fees. I will put 100 jin of compound and about 80 jin of urea total on each mu of wheat. I irrigate three times: when the wheat wakes up after winter, at heading, and when the grain is filling. I spray four times — herbicide once at the start, insecticide twice, and fungicide once. I use the rotary tiller before planting. The seed is improved wheat, the same kind my neighbor used last year with good results.

For maize, I plant it right after the wheat comes off in June. There is no time to plough — I plant directly into the wheat stubble. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer in the row when I plant. That is the 28-6-6 kind. I add about 25 jin of urea later when the plants are knee-high if they look like they need it. Maize needs less fuss than wheat. I irrigate twice, and I spray three times — herbicide once and insecticide twice. I use Denghai 605 hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses it because it gives heavy grain.

The cotton is on 12 mu on the east side of my land. Cotton needs more work and more spraying. I put 100 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu before planting. Cotton needs potash or the bolls drop off — my cousin learned that the hard way — so I make sure the fertilizer has all three numbers. I spray insecticide 12 times through the season for bollworm. If you skip even one spray, the worms will eat the whole crop. I irrigate twice. I till with the rotary tiller first. The seed is an improved variety called Guoxinmian, same as last year.

My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in the city, so at harvest time I hire people to help. Sixty mu is too much for me and my husband alone. Diesel for the pump and wages for the harvesters are my biggest costs after fertilizer. I watch what my neighbors do, and they watch me. If everyone around here applies a certain amount, I do something similar. Change is risky. I would rather do what I did last year and get a safe crop than try something new and lose everything.
